text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament member Musallam al-Barak says will not forget "Khartoum's negative position." Kuwait received a Sudanese minister on Tuesday for the first time since Iraq's 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait, during which Khartoum showed sympathy with Baghdad angering the Gulf Arab state.
- Parliamentary committee suspends Kuwait municipality's budget proposal.
- Judge extends detention of five suspects held in connection with a failed assassination attempt against opposition MP Abdullah al-Naibari in June.
- Kuwait wants Gulf Arab states to unify electricity and water charges.
- About 141 million shares worth 46.5 million dinars ($154 million) changed hands on the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

- MP expects the state to naturalise residents born to Kuwaiti mothers from stateless fathers. Kuwait is home to about 110,000 stateless people who claim to be Kuwaitis, while the state says they are illegal residents who have concealed their original nationality documents.
- More leave, more indemnity in draft labour law.
- Call for banning motorists from using mobile telephones.
